purpose: Test deterministic temporal replay with duplicate deliveries, corrections, retractions, conflicts and UNKNOWN boundaries.

activities.label: deduplicate and preserve an append-only evidence ledger
replay multiple arrival permutations into a deterministic projection
attack temporal authority, conflict, duplicate and retraction invariants

queries.expression: does replay produce the same projection under reordered arrival
does correction retract a fact without deleting its evidence history
do conflicts remain conflicts and insufficient temporal authority remain UNKNOWN

assumptions: The source version is authoritative for ordering state assertions within this synthetic source.
valid_time and observed_at are distinct clocks and are not interchangeable.
A retraction names the event it corrects and does not erase that event from the ledger.
Two distinct values at the same source version cannot be silently resolved.
This first slice replays a finite batch and does not claim live stream guarantees.
kill_tests: A set event without source version or valid time blocks instead of becoming a fact.
A retraction naming an unknown event blocks.
A same-version conflict cannot collapse to one value.
Removing a retraction fails the history invariant.
An UNKNOWN observation cannot be promoted to SUPPORTED without temporal authority.
An event version ahead of the source version blocks.
unknowns: How watermarks and late events should work in a live connector.
How to handle partitioned streams and concurrent source versions.
Whether a source version is sufficient or a causal clock is required for each application.
How to make the projection atomic with an external action under TOCTOU.
How this batch contract maps to OpenEMR and Nextcloud temporal models.
